paraphrase: Deluding karma (mohanīya) is named as view-deluding (darśana-mohanīya), conduct-deluding (cāritra-mohanīya), non-passion-felt (akaṣāya-vedanīya) and passion-felt (kaṣāya-vedanīya), with three, two, nine and sixteen kinds respectively. View-deluding: right view (samyaktva), wrong view (mithyātva) and both (tad-ubhaya). Conduct-deluding: non-passion and passion (akaṣāya, kaṣāya). Non-passions: laughter, liking, disliking, grief, fear, disgust, and the female, male and neuter sex-drive (vedas). The passions are the four, anger (krodha), pride (māna), deceit (māyā) and greed (lobha), each with four varieties (vikalpa) named anantānubandhī ("bound to the endless"), apratyākhyāna ("non-renunciation"), pratyākhyāna ("renunciation") and saṃjvalana ("flaring together"); these glosses give only the literal sense of the names.
speaker: Umāsvāti (author of the sūtra, by tradition)
notes: The sūtra names the four passions and the four varieties (anantānubandhī, apratyākhyāna, pratyākhyāna, saṃjvalana) and gives the counts 3, 2, 9, 16 (four passions times four varieties is sixteen); the varieties are not defined in the sūtra. In the Digambara commentarial line (Sarvārthasiddhi) the varieties are read as the passion that binds for endless saṃsāra, that hinders partial restraint, that hinders complete restraint, and that smoulders alongside restraint; that is the commentators' reading, not the sūtra's words.
